records.title: Pre-arrest bail refused to alleged go-between after a police raid on a Visakhapatnam hotel room
records.case_reference: Crl.P. No. 5787 of 2026 (Crime No. 147 of 2026, Airport Police Station, Visakhapatnam)
records.summary: Police raided a Visakhapatnam hotel on a tip-off, found a man and a woman in a room, and charged the people said to have arranged the meeting for Rs 1,500 under human-trafficking and brothel laws. On 4 August 2026 the High Court refused pre-arrest bail to the man accused of linking customers to the organiser.
detail: According to the prosecution case recorded by the High Court, on 13 June 2026 the Inspector of Police, Airport Police Station, Visakhapatnam, acting 'on receipt of credible information regarding prostitution activities', raided a hotel at Madhavadhara and found 'a man and a woman' in a room 'allegedly engaged in prostitution'. The customer had been arranged 'after collecting Rs.1,500/- towards sexual services'. Two mobile phones and Rs 500 were seized.

Police registered Crime No. 147 of 2026 under sections 143(3) and 144(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the new code's human-trafficking provisions, and sections 3, 4 and 5 of the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, which punish keeping a brothel, living on the earnings of sex work and procuring.

The petitioner, accused no. 4, argued that the only evidence against him was a co-accused's confession and that the raid was not led by a special police officer as the Immoral Traffic Act requires. The State replied that the legality of the raid was a matter for trial.

Justice Y. Lakshmana Rao held that the case record showed the petitioner 'acted as a crucial person in running the brothel by luring customers and coordinating between the customers and the organiser', noted that 'there are no adverse antecedents reported against the petitioner', and dismissed the petition.
records.current_position: Pre-arrest bail refused on 4 August 2026 while the investigation continued. We have not located any later order.

quote.heading: What the High Court said
quote.text: In view of the specific overt acts attributed against the petitioner, this Court is not inclined to grant pre-arrest bail to the petitioner, as it would amount to giving a shield, protection or licence to the petitioner in respect of the specific allegations levelled against him
quote.where: Crl.P. No. 5787 of 2026, order dated 4 August 2026, para 14

sections.label: Why it is listed
sections.heading: A paid encounter, charged as trafficking
sections.text: The order describes a paid sexual encounter arranged by phone, found by police acting on a tip-off. It records no complaint by anyone involved and no allegation of force, deception or a minor, yet police charged the people who arranged it under human-trafficking and brothel-keeping laws.

records.caveats: The order does not give the ages of the man and woman found in the room. It refers to the statements of 'the other victims', the term trafficking law uses for anyone in sex work, without describing what they said.

sources.publisher: High Court of Andhra Pradesh (via Indian Kanoon)
sources.supports: the raid, charges, arguments, the court's reasons and the refusal of bail

One of them was convicted on 10 June 2025, the High Court recorded on 15 September 2026 when it closed his petition to quash the case.
detail: In 2024 G. Sigadam police registered Crime No. 120 of 2024 under section 112(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and section 3 read with section 4 of the Andhra Pradesh Gaming Act, 1974. Justice Maheswara Rao Kuncheam closed the petition. The order does not give the sentence or say which of the charged sections the conviction was under.

records.title: Man detained without trial as a 'bootlegger' over liquor cases in which he already had bail; High Court orders release
records.authority: Collector and District Magistrate, Nandyal (detention); High Court of Andhra Pradesh (set aside)
records.case_reference: W.P. No. 29381 of 2025; detention order dated 24 July 2025; G.O.Rt. No. 1614, General Administration (SC-I) Department, dated 3 September 2025
laws: Section 2(b) ('bootlegger'), Andhra Pradesh Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Dacoits, Drug Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders and Land Grabbers Act, 1986
Andhra Pradesh Prohibition Act, 1995 (four underlying cases)
acts: Andhra Pradesh Prevention of Dangerous Activities Act, 1986
records.person: A man from Panyam; his wife brought the petition
records.summary: Nandyal's district collector ordered a man detained without trial as a 'bootlegger' because of four cases against him under the prohibition law, in every one of which courts had already granted him bail. The state confirmed the detention in September 2025. On 5 May 2026 the High Court set the order aside and directed his release.
detail: On 24 July 2025 the Collector and District Magistrate of Nandyal ordered the preventive detention of the petitioner's husband, treating him as a 'bootlegger' under section 2(b) of the 1986 preventive-detention law. The High Court recorded that 'about four crimes were registered against the detenu for the offences punishable under the A.P. Prohibition Act' and that 'conditional bail was granted to him in all the said four crimes'.

The detaining authority reasoned that his repeated offences were 'prejudicial to the maintenance of public order and posing danger to public safety and health'. The State confirmed the order by G.O.Rt. No. 1614 on 3 September 2025, 'and since then he has been in custody', the court recorded.

A Division Bench of Justices Cheekati Manavendranath Roy and Tuhin Kumar Gedela held that the bail orders, and the effect of their conditions, had not been placed before and weighed by the detaining authority, which 'invalidates the order of preventive detention'. It set the order aside and directed that he 'be released forthwith'.
The judgment records no allegation of violence, of spurious or poisonous liquor, or of harm to any person. The only conduct it mentions is repeated offences under the prohibition law.
records.current_position: Detention set aside on 5 May 2026 and release ordered. The four Prohibition Act cases themselves are not described in the judgment.

quote.heading: What the High Court recorded
quote.text: About four crimes were registered against the detenu for the offences punishable under the A.P. Prohibition Act. Conditional bail was granted to him in all the said four crimes.
quote.where: W.P. No. 29381 of 2025, judgment dated 5 May 2026, para 3

sections.label: Why it is listed
sections.heading: Jail without trial for selling drink
sections.text: Preventive detention lets the state imprison a person for up to a year without a trial. Here it was used against a man whose only recorded conduct was liquor offences, after courts had released him on bail in each of them.

records.caveats: The judgment does not say what the four Prohibition Act cases involved (quantities, or whether liquor was sold or only possessed), or the exact date he was taken into custody.

sources.publisher: High Court of Andhra Pradesh (via Indian Kanoon)
sources.supports: the detention and confirmation orders, the four Prohibition Act cases and bail, the court's reasons and the release order

records.title: Beef trader's licence cancelled by text message; High Court suspends the cancellation
records.authority: Vizianagaram Municipal Corporation (cancellation); High Court of Andhra Pradesh (interim suspension)
records.case_reference: W.P. No. 16293 of 2025; trade licence No. TL/03809/20
laws: Municipal trade licence (the order does not cite the statute)
records.summary: Vizianagaram's municipal corporation cancelled a beef trader's licence with a text message to his phone on 6 June 2025, without notice or reasons. It later said he had not produced receipts showing he bought his beef from a licensed supplier. On 3 July 2025 the High Court suspended the cancellation.
detail: The High Court recorded that the trader's licence was cancelled 'on the basis of a message to the mobile number of the Petitioner on 06.06.2025'. His counsel said no prior notice was issued and no reasons were given.

On written instructions, the corporation's standing counsel told the court that the Municipal Health Officer had reported that the trader 'failed to furnish receipts for procurement of beef from Vizag Foods Private Limited', and that complaints had been received of unauthorised slaughter of cows and buffaloes 'by certain traders' in the Cantonment area.

The court held that because cancelling the licence had civil consequences, the trader should have been given notice first. It suspended the cancellation for four weeks and left the corporation free to issue notice about the complaints.
records.current_position: Cancellation suspended for four weeks from 3 July 2025; the case was listed for 31 July 2025. We have not located any later order.

quote.heading: What the High Court said
quote.text: as there are civil consequences for cancellation of the trade license of the Petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, the Petitioner should have been put on notice before taking any action in this regard.
quote.where: W.P. No. 16293 of 2025, order dated 3 July 2025

sections.label: Why it is listed
sections.heading: A livelihood switched off by SMS
sections.text: Selling beef harms no one who does not choose to buy it. The trader's licence, and with it his business, was cancelled by text message over paperwork about where his meat came from.

records.caveats: The order does not say whether the trader himself was accused of slaughtering cattle; the slaughter complaints it mentions concern 'certain traders' in the area. More recent 2026 cattle cases in the state were not used for this category because they also charge cruelty to animals during transport.

records.title: Rs 2 lakh food-safety fine in a tobacco case set aside nine years later
records.authority: Joint Collector-cum-Adjudicating Officer, Guntur (penalty); High Court of Andhra Pradesh (set aside)
records.case_reference: Crl.R.C. No. 210 of 2019; Crl.A. No. 100 of 2018 (Principal District and Sessions Judge, Guntur); Rc. No. 1024/2017-L.2
laws: Section 96, Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006
records.penalty: Rs 2,00,000, reduced to Rs 70,000 on appeal; both set aside
records.summary: In November 2017 Guntur's joint collector fined a Macherla man Rs 2 lakh under the food-safety law; on appeal the fine was cut to Rs 70,000. On 6 August 2026 the High Court set both orders aside, applying its settled view that chewing tobacco and khaini are not 'food', so the food-safety law cannot be used to punish trade in them.
detail: The High Court recorded that on 16 November 2017 the Joint Collector-cum-Adjudicating Officer, Guntur, imposed a penalty of Rs 2,00,000 on the petitioner under section 96 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. On appeal, the Principal District and Sessions Judge, Guntur, reduced it to Rs 70,000 on 30 January 2019.

The petitioner's counsel relied on earlier High Court rulings that chewing tobacco and khaini are not food within the Act, and that trade in tobacco is governed by the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act, 2003, not the food-safety law. One of those rulings, quoted in the order, notes that 'the trade in Tobacco is not impermissible in India'.

Justice Y. Lakshmana Rao held that, 'in view of the constant view taken by this Court', the Sessions judgment and the collector's order were 'liable to be interfered and set aside', and set both aside on 6 August 2026.
records.current_position: Penalty set aside on 6 August 2026, nearly nine years after it was imposed.

quote.heading: The rule the High Court applied
quote.text: chewing tobacco and khaini are not the food within the definition of Section 3(j) of 'the Act.,' and the manufacture, sale or exposing for sale of tobacco etc., is governed by the provisions of the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003
quote.where: Crl.R.C. No. 210 of 2019, order dated 6 August 2026, para 4 (recording an earlier order of the High Court)

sections.label: Why it is listed
sections.heading: A fine for a lawful trade
sections.text: Tobacco is a legal product in India. The man was fined under a law the High Court has repeatedly held does not apply to it, and it took nine years and three levels of adjudication to undo.

records.caveats: The order does not describe the goods or the conduct that was penalised. That the case concerned tobacco products follows from the ground on which the High Court decided it. Macherla is now in Palnadu district; the order refers to Guntur district.

sources.publisher: High Court of Andhra Pradesh (via Indian Kanoon)
sources.supports: the 2017 penalty, the 2019 appeal, the legal ground and the setting aside

records.title: Police charged a Visakhapatnam shopkeeper with 'poisoning' for storing e-cigarettes; High Court quashes the case
records.authority: Visakhapatnam City police (prosecution); High Court of Andhra Pradesh (quashed)
records.case_reference: Crl.P. No. 12896 of 2025; C.C. No. 2896 of 2025 (IV Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Visakhapatnam); FIR No. 57 of 2024, III Town Police Station
laws: Section 5 read with section 8, Prohibition of Electronic Cigarettes Act, 2019
records.summary: In March 2024 Visakhapatnam's City Task Force raided shops selling e-cigarettes and charged a shopkeeper not only under the e-cigarette ban but under penal-code sections for negligence with poison and for causing hurt by poison. On 9 March 2026 the High Court quashed the whole prosecution: e-cigarettes are not 'poison', and the storage offence is non-cognizable, so police could not file a charge sheet for it.
detail: The Hindu reported on 24 March 2024 that Visakhapatnam's City Task Force raided two shops, arrested two people for selling banned e-cigarettes, and seized several hundred of them.

III Town police registered FIR No. 57 of 2024 under section 5 read with section 8 of the Prohibition of Electronic Cigarettes Act, 2019, which bans storing e-cigarettes, and under sections 284 and 328 of the Indian Penal Code, which punish negligent conduct with poisonous substances and causing hurt by poison. A charge sheet followed, and the case was numbered C.C. No. 2896 of 2025.

Justice Y. Lakshmana Rao held that e-cigarettes are not a 'poisonous substance' under section 284, and that the facts alleged did not amount to administering poison under section 328. He further held that the storage offence under the e-cigarette law is non-cognizable, so it had to be pursued by a written complaint from an authorised officer, not a police charge sheet. The proceedings were quashed.
records.current_position: Prosecution quashed by the High Court on 9 March 2026.

quote.heading: What the High Court held
quote.text: Electronic cigarettes, which form the subject matter of the present prosecution, do not, by any legally tenable construction or judicial interpretation, answer the description of a 'poisonous substance' within the contemplation of Section 284 of 'the I.P.C.,' nor do the facts alleged constitute the administration of poison or stupefying substances as envisaged under Section 328 of 'the I.P.C.'
quote.where: Crl.P. No. 12896 of 2025, judgment dated 9 March 2026, para 6

sections.label: Why it is listed
sections.heading: Storing a product, charged as poisoning
sections.text: Adults who buy e-cigarettes choose to. The shopkeeper was prosecuted for keeping them in stock, and police added poisoning charges that the High Court found had no legal basis.

records.caveats: The judgment gives the FIR number but not the date of the raid; the date is taken from The Hindu's report, which gives the number seized as both 734 and 743. The Hindu report mentions two shops; the judgment concerns one accused.

records.title: Woman on hunger strike to meet the Chief Minister booked for attempted suicide
records.authority: Kakinada Urban police, on a complaint by the Mandal Executive Magistrate; recorded by the High Court of Andhra Pradesh
records.case_reference: Cr. No. 80 of 2023 (section 309 read with 34 IPC); W.P. No. 21912 of 2023 (High Court)
laws: Section 309 read with section 34, Indian Penal Code, 1860
records.summary: A Kakinada woman in a property dispute with two police constables went on hunger strike after being refused a meeting with the Chief Minister. According to the State, she was taken to hospital when her health deteriorated, tried to take her own life there, and was then booked for attempted suicide on the complaint of the local executive magistrate. On 6 January 2026 the High Court directed police not to interfere with her liberty except by due process.
detail: The woman petitioned the High Court alleging that police officers were harassing her and her disabled daughter and pressing her to settle a property dispute with two police constables on their terms, including by admitting the two of them to a mental hospital in Visakhapatnam.

The Assistant Government Pleader, on instructions, told the court that the Chief Minister's security staff did not allow her to meet the Chief Minister at his camp office; that when she sat on hunger strike a medical team advised shifting her to the Government Hospital as her health was deteriorating; and that she 'tried to commit suicide' after admission. On the complaint of the Mandal Executive Magistrate, Kakinada Urban, a case was registered under section 309 read with section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, the offence of attempting suicide.

Justice Venkata Jyothirmai Pratapa disposed of the petition by directing the respondents 'not to interfere with the personal liberty of the petitioner and her daughter, except under due process of law'. The order does not deal with the attempted-suicide case itself.

Section 115 of the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 provides that a person who attempts suicide is presumed, unless proved otherwise, to have severe stress, and shall not be tried and punished under section 309.
records.current_position: The attempted-suicide case (Cr. No. 80 of 2023) was registered; its present status is not stated in the High Court order.

quote.heading: What the State told the High Court
quote.text: On the complaint made by the Mandal Executive Magistrate, Kakinada Urban regarding the petitioner's attempt to commit suicide, a case in Cr.No.80 of 2023 was registered u/s 309 r/w 34 IPC.
quote.where: W.P. No. 21912 of 2023, order dated 6 January 2026, para 4

sections.label: Why it is listed
sections.heading: Prosecuted for her own distress
sections.text: The only person the alleged act could have harmed was the woman herself. Parliament has said such a person should be presumed to be under severe stress and not punished, yet a criminal case was registered against her on an official's complaint.

records.caveats: The facts about the hunger strike and the suicide attempt are the State's account, given on instructions; they were not tested by the court. The order does not give the date of the incident or say whether the case has been charge-sheeted or closed. If you or someone you know is struggling, Tele-MANAS (14416) offers free support.

records.title: Shop owner prosecuted in Nawada for alleged obscene video show
records.summary: The Circle Officer raided a house in Roh and arrested two workers over alleged obscene pictures and videos. The Judicial Magistrate at Nawada took cognizance against a local shop owner under obscenity law and cinema law. The High Court recorded that two case-diary witnesses supported the allegation and dismissed the plea to quash the cognizance order.
records.authority: Patna High Court (Justice [name withheld]); Judicial Magistrate First Class, Nawada; Circle Officer, Roh
records.case_reference: CR. MISC. No. 34235 of 2016; Roh P.S. Case No. 50 of 2013
records.person: a cloth-shop owner in Roh, Nawada district, alleged to have run the video show
detail: The High Court recorded that the petition sought setting aside the Magistrate's cognizance order dated 02.01.2016 in Roh P.S. Case No. 50 of 2013 under obscenity and cinema law.

The High Court recorded that the allegation was that obscene pictures and videos were being played in a house, and that the Circle Officer raided the house and arrested two employees of the alleged operator.
The High Court recorded that the petitioner's counsel said the police chargesheet had exonerated the petitioner, that he owned a saree shop, and that no witness spoke against him.

The High Court recorded that the State opposed the plea, submitting that two prosecution witnesses named in paragraphs 7 and 8 of the case diary supported the case and the cognizance order was correct.

The High Court held that the final report in the petitioner's favour was not sufficient to exonerate him, that the offences were prima facie attracted on the case-diary material, and dismissed the petition.
records.current_position: The quashing petition was dismissed, so the cognizance order stands and the prosecution is to proceed before the Magistrate.

records.title: Customer found in hotel room during vice raid faced prosecution under vice and trafficking laws
records.summary: Police raided a lodging hotel and prosecuted a man found in a room with a woman as a customer under the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act and trafficking law. The High Court recorded that the victim's statement was never recorded and only police statements were relied on. The Court set aside the refusal to discharge him.
records.case_reference: Criminal Revision Application No. 347/2023, Sessions Case No. 24/2015 arising out of C.R. No. II 56/2014, Manpada Police Station
laws: Sections 3, 4 and 5 of the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956
Section 370(3) of the Indian Penal Code
records.person: a customer found in a lodging hotel room in the Thane area
detail: The High Court recorded that the FIR was registered on 29/10/2014 after police raided a lodging and boarding hotel on 28/10/2014 at about 8.15 p.m. on the allegation that prostitution activities were being carried out there.
The High Court recorded that the applicant was accused no. 5 and was alleged to be a customer found in a room with the woman named in the panchnama, with cash of Rs 250 found with the woman.
The High Court recorded that the State informed the Court that the statement of the victim was not recorded and the only material was the statement of raiding police officials.

The High Court held that Sections 3 and 4 of the PITA and Section 370 of the IPC were not attracted on those facts and set aside the Sessions Court order dated 25/8/2023 that had rejected discharge, allowing the revision for the applicant only.
records.current_position: The prosecution under Sections 3, 4, 5 of PITA and Section 370 IPC does not continue against the customer following the High Court order.

quote.text: In my view, Sections 3 and 4 of the PITA as well as Section 370 of the IPC are not at all attracted in the present facts as the applicant is alleged to be a customer and as the statement of the victim is not recorded.

records.caveats: Victim age and consent were not established by a victim statement; the Court decided on the absence of material. Trial status of co-accused was not confirmed.

sections.label: Why it is listed
sections.heading: No complaining victim
sections.text: Paid sex between adults involved no complaining victim, no minor, and no allegation of force or deception against the customer, so prosecution punished a victimless arrangement.

records.title: Nine persons raided for playing cards on street face gambling prosecution

records.case_reference: Criminal Application (APL) No. 578 of 2022, FIR No. 0368/2019, Police Station Umarkhed
laws: Section 12(A) of the Maharashtra Prevention of Gambling Act, 1887
records.person: persons found playing cards on a street in Umarkhed

The High Court recorded that a spot panchnama was drawn, playing cards and amounts were recovered, and the investigating officer filed a charge-sheet after investigation.
The High Court recorded that the FIR recitals showed the persons were found gaming with cards and cash at a street where the public have access, making prima facie material for Section 12(a).

records.title: Landlord prosecuted after liquor meant for sale in Haryana stored in his rented room
records.summary: Excise officers raided a house and seized foreign liquor meant for sale in Haryana but kept in Maharashtra, charging six persons under the Prohibition Act. The landlord said he had let the room only for electrical goods. The High Court quashed the FIR and charge-sheet against the landlord.
records.case_reference: Criminal Application (APL) No. 107/2025, Crime No. 110/2024 dated 26.10.2024, Police Station Jaripatka; Summary Criminal Case No. 925/2025
laws: Sections 65(a)(e), 81, 83, 90 and 98 of the Maharashtra Prohibition Act, 1949
records.person: a landlord in Nagpur whose rented room was used to store liquor
detail: The High Court recorded that the Excise Inspector reported that liquor for sale in Haryana and banned in Maharashtra was stored at the applicant's house, and a raid during loading of a vehicle led to recovery and confiscation.

The High Court recorded that the applicant said he was only the landlord who had given a small ground-floor room on leave and licence from 01/11/2023 to 31/07/2026 for storing electrical items, without consent for liquor storage.

The High Court recorded that Sections 65(a) and (e) punish import, export, transport, sale, purchase or possession of intoxicant, but the applicant's role was limited to being landlord, so no offence was made out even on FIR facts.
The High Court allowed the application and quashed the FIR and charge-sheet to the extent of the landlord applicant.
records.current_position: The case is quashed for the landlord; the position of the other accused was not decided in this order.

quote.text: As can be seen from the above clauses that the role of the applicant is limited to he being a landlord of the premises in question.

records.caveats: Quantity of liquor seized and proof of Haryana-only sale marking beyond FIR recitals were not confirmed; no chemical report of spurious liquor was mentioned.

sections.label: Why it is listed
sections.heading: No complaining victim
sections.text: Possessing, carrying and storing drinkable liquor involved no spurious liquor, hooch death, violence, or complaining victim.

records.title: Van occupants prosecuted for carrying bones with dried flesh under cattle law
records.summary: Police stopped a pick-up van on a road and seized 15 kg of raw bones with dried flesh, arresting the driver and naming two others. The FIR charged only the cattle-preservation law. The High Court kept the flesh-possession charge alive while quashing the sale charge.
records.case_reference: Criminal Application (APL) No. 597 of 2025, FIR No. 0076 of 2025 dated 23.02.2025, Akot Police Station
laws: Sections 5B, 5C and 9 of the Maharashtra Animal Preservation Act, 1976
records.person: a driver and two occupants of a pick-up van on a road near Akot
detail: The High Court recorded that police on patrol near Shivneri Dhaba road stopped a Mahindra pick-up van, arrested the driver, and were told by him that the vehicle contained raw bones.

The High Court recorded that the panchnama showed raw bones with traces of dried flesh weighing 15 kg worth about Rs 30,000 were seized, and an animal husbandry report said the bones were of matured large bovine.
The High Court recorded that the FIR invoked only Sections 5B, 5C and 9 of the 1976 Act, with no Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, theft, or violence charge.
The High Court held Section 5B was not attracted but Section 5C possession of flesh was prima facie attracted, so prosecution continues for Section 5C.
records.current_position: The FIR is quashed only for Section 5B; prosecution under Section 5C of the cattle-preservation law continues.

quote.text: the raw bones with the trace of dried flesh on bones of total weight of 15kg having approximate costs of Rs.30,000/- was found and they were seized.

records.caveats: Species as cow versus buffalo beyond large bovine opinion and forensic confirmation were not confirmed; live-cattle transport or slaughter was not alleged.

sections.heading: No complaining victim
sections.text: Possessing bovine flesh for food or trade harmed no person, with no cruelty, theft, or violence charge in the case.
